item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox enter Tuesday night’s series opener against the Cleveland Guardians having already clinched a postseason berth and holding an 84-72 overall record.
Ahead of the matchup, however, Red Sox manager Chad Tracy, who had the interim tag removed prior to the game, made some notable changes to his starting lineup. One of those changes features former All-Star outfielder Jarren Duran.
Red Sox Make Duran Move
The last time we saw Boston take the field was Sunday, when the Red Sox lost 5-1 against the Tampa Bay Rays and Duran went 0-for-3 at the plate with a walk.
Despite having the day off on Monday, it seems Tracy is committing to platooning Duran more down the stretch amid his struggles this season, as he’s out of the starting lineup for Tuesday’s game.
This comes while both Ceddanne Rafaela and Eli White remain sidelined as well, which is all the more concerning for Duran’s status moving forward. When Rafaela returns, he’ll move back to center field, and with Roman Anthony in left and Wilyer Abreu in right, Duran is the odd man out in this setting.
Here’s the Red Sox starting lineup vs. Guardians:
Via Underdog MLB: “Red Sox 9/22 R. Anthony LF N. Sogard 1B J. Jones DH W. Abreu RF A. Rutschman C C. Durbin 3B A. Monasterio 2B I. Kiner-Falefa SS N. Eaton CF P. Tolle SP.”
Red Sox 9/22
R. Anthony LF
N. Sogard 1B
J. Jones DH
W. Abreu RF
A. Rutschman C
C. Durbin 3B
A. Monasterio 2B
I. Kiner-Falefa SS
N. Eaton CF
P. Tolle SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 22, 2026
Duran’s 2026 Season
In his sixth MLB season, Duran simply hasn’t found the consistency he hoped for at the plate, despite putting up solid home run and RBI numbers.
Duran has appeared in 145 games for Boston this year and is hitting just .204 with 65 runs, 110 hits, 20 home runs, and 69 RBIs while slugging .362 with a .624 OPS.

item.content:encoded:
A falta de una semana para que termine la temporada regular en la MLB, el panorama de playoffs comienza a definirse y con ello te presentamos aquellos peloteros mexicanos que ya aseguraron su clasificación a playoffs y quienes todavía están en la pelea por entrar a la postemporada.
Mexicanos que ya aseguraron su pase a postemporada
La presencia de peloteros mexicanos en las últimas ediciones de los playoffs ha sido constante y este año no será la excepción pues hasta ahorita se tiene confirmada la participación de cuatro peloteros mexicanos y dos con estatus todavía pendiente, ya que uno está en sucursales y el otro se encuentra en lista de lesionados.
PUBLICIDAD
A continuación, te presentamos la lista de jugadores nacionales que estarán en los playoffs:
Jonathan Aranda (Tampa Bay Rays)
Ha firmado su campaña más sólida y consagratoria en MLB. Con 149 juegos jugados, el infielder presume un promedio de bateo de .277, conectando 156 imparables, 22 cuadrangulares y remolcando 92 carreras, convirtiéndose en una pieza medular en el lineup de los Rays.
Jarren Durán (Boston Red Sox):
Se ha consolidado como un auténtico motor en los senderos y el jardín central. A lo largo de la temporada suma 20 jonrones, 69 carreras impulsadas y 19 bases robadas en 145 encuentros, destacando además por su velocidad con 5 triples.
PUBLICIDAD
Joey Ortiz (Milwaukee Brewers):
Ha sido una de las grandes revelaciones del año tras su llegada a Milwaukee, aportando una defensa de élite en el cuadro y un bateo sumamente oportuno que ayudó a los Brewers a amarrar temprano su boleto a octubre.
Patrick Sandoval (Boston Red Sox):
El lanzador que representó a México en el Clásico Mundial de Beisbol regresó esta temporada tras un periodo largo fuera de las canchas y ha tenido altibajos con los Boston Red Sox con una efectividad de 5.15 y un récord de 1-7.
Manuel Rodríguez (Tampa Bay Rays):
El lanzador yucateco venía sumando valiosos relevos con efectividad de 3.86 y 8 ponches en el bullpen de Tampa Bay en los cuatro juegos que disputó.
PUBLICIDAD
No obstante, Manuel Rodríguez se encuentra actualmente en la lista de lesionados (IL) de 15 días debido a una distensión en la espalda baja (low back strain), por lo que el cuerpo técnico espera su evolución para ver si podrá estar listo en las primeras rondas de los playoffs.
Alek Thomas (Oklahoma City Comets):
Después de haber sido cambiado desde los Arizona Diamondbacks a inicios de año, el jardinero Alek Thomas se encuentra actualmente en las sucursales de Los Angeles Dodgers
Aunque tuvo una breve participación de 7 juegos con el primer equipo de los Dodgers bateando para .211, la tremenda profundidad del roster angelino ha hecho que se mantenga buscando ritmo en el sistema de ligas menores, a la espera de un llamado que lo devuelva al roster de postemporada.
PUBLICIDAD
Peloteros mexicanos todavía buscan entrar a la postemporada
La presencia de peloteros mexicanos aumentará conforme avance la semana, con varios representantes en equipos que continúan en competencia por buscar entrar a los playoffs.
Toronto Blue Jays cuenta con Alejandro Kirk, Tibo Rodríguez, Brandon Valenzuela y Luis Urías. Por su parte, Randy Arozarena y Andrés Muñoz forman parte de los Seattle Mariners.
Isaac Paredes representa a los Houston Astros, mientras Javier Assad se encuentra con los Chicago Cubs. Alejandro Osuna integra el roster de los Texas Rangers.
Taijuan Walker juega con los Philadelphia Phillies y Jeremiah Estrada pertenece a los San Diego Padres.
Cada uno luchará hasta el último segundo por entrar a la postemporada.
PUBLICIDAD

item.content:encoded:
RedSoxRoundtable's Zach Coe discusses whether or not the Red Sox have enough offensive firepower to win a World Series on the 'Bleav in Boston' podcast. Be sure to join our FREE community over on RedSoxRoundtable.com!
The Boston Red Sox have a well-documented outfield logjam, with Jarren Duran, Ceddanne Rafaela, Wilyer Abreu, and Roman Anthony. But could the team be preparing to add another piece to the already confusing puzzle? At least one person thinks so, as Seattle Mariners beat reporter Ryan Divish linked pending free-agent Randy Arozarena to Boston in an appearance on the 'Foul Territory' podcast.
What did Divish say?
"They're [Seattle] going to lose their best player. Randy Arozarena is going to be a free agent. I think we all know Randy would probably prefer to stay on the East Coast," Divish said. "I'm guessing Boston is ready to cut a huge check for him," he continued.
Is Arozarena a fit?
From a sheer production perspective, the 31-year-old could be the missing piece for a Red Sox offense that still feels a bat short. Arozarena is coming off the best two seasons of his career, hitting .258/.355/.453/.808 with 53 home runs, 63 doubles, and 152 RBI en route to back-to-back All-Star selections, all while playing half of his games in one of the most pitcher-friendly environments in the sport, Seattle's T-Mobile Park.
Arozarena has also had incredible success at Fenway Park, posting a .278/.351/.481/.833 slash line with five home runs, 12 doubles, and 19 RBI in career 32 games. He also fits the profile of hitters that Boston has targeted under Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow, pulling the ball in the air at a consistent rate. Along with a strong track record at Fenway Park, Arozarena has proven himself in the postseason, hitting .292/.380/.565/.946 in 45 playoff games, including being named ALCS Most Valuable Player in 2020 with the Tampa Bay Rays.
However, bringing in the veteran outfielder would require significant roster reshuffling, including moving both an outfielder and the designated hitter, Masataka Yoshida.
Our take
If Arozarena is set on returning to the East Coast, he could be the perfect fit for the Red Sox offense. His defensive metrics at this stage of his career suggest he's best suited as a designated hitter, and the Red Sox have gotten some of the worst production in baseball from their revolving door of designated hitters in 2026. He also has a proven track record of success at both Fenway Park and in the postseason.
While signing him would require some roster maneuvering, including potentially selling Duran at his lowest possible value or eating the $18.6 million remaining on Masataka Yoshida's contract, Arozarena is about as perfect fit as you can get for the Red Sox in what's set to be a weak class of free-agent bats, especially if the offense comes up short in the playoffs for the second consecutive season.
Up next for the Sox
After clinching a playoff berth on Sunday afternoon, the Red Sox are off on Monday before opening up the final homestand of the regular season on Tuesday, welcoming the Cleveland Guardians to Fenway Park for a three-game set. Payton Tolle (9-6, 3.02 ERA) will get the start opposite fellow rookie left-hander Parker Messick (12-9, 2.57 ERA) for Cleveland. First pitch is set for 6:45 p.m. ET.

item.content:encoded:
The Yankees’ odds of winning the AL East are down to 2.8 percent per FanGraphs after getting walked off by the Diamondbacks last night. I know mathematically that makes sense, but the chances mentally feel even more extreme. I’ve been having “fun” (or whatever) comping the odds to certain pitchers from history getting a hit. We are the dregs. Remember mid-2000s Mets pitcher Aaron Heilman? I personally remember him most for giving up the homer to Yadier Molina late in Game 7 of the 2006 NLCS, just before Adam Wainwright famously caught Carlos Beltrán looking to win the pennant.
Anyway, Heilman was a horrendous hitter. He singled once in his rookie year, and then never got another hit. He ended his career 1-for-47, so an .021 average. So the Yankees just need magic only a little bit more sufficient than that RBI single by Heilman off Sidney Ponson on August 12, 2003! Hell yeah.
It’s not happening, but we press on because it’s good to check up on what everyone else is doing anyway. Here’s what was going on Saturday.
Tampa Bay Rays (94-60) 2, Boston Red Sox (84-71) 1
The Yankees gained a full game on the Rays on Friday for the first time in over a week, as Boston snapped their six-game winning streak. There was no such fortune to be found yesterday though; Tampa Bay made sure of that well before first pitch in Arizona, and it only got worse from there. By the end of the night, the Rays once again had a five-game lead over the Yanks; Tampa Bay’s magic number (combination of Rays wins or Yankees losses) to clinch the AL East is four.
This one was a pitchers’ duel to the bitter end. Brayan Bello had easily his best outing of a turbulent season (and probably the best of his career), firing eight shutout frames at the Trop and fanning 11 Rays, tying a personal best from July 9, 2024. As he only went 5.1 in that one and faced merely the soon-to-depart-Oakland A’s rather than the division-leading Rays.
The only true blemish on Bello’s record came when Jonathan Aranda cracked an opposite-field homer to make it a 1-1 game in the fourth. Tampa Bay had a chance to make it 2-1 against Bello in the seventh when Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson led off with singles. Bello then induced a grounder from Victor Mesa Jr. to move up the runners, and then another off the bat of Richie Palacios to Trevor Story, who nailed pinch-runner Jonny DeLuca at home. Palacios swiped second, but Bello fanned Cedric Mullins to end the inning. The Rays went down in order in the eighth to end Bello’s brilliant night.
Unfortunately for Bello, a win wasn’t in the cards because Boston put up next to nothing against Freddy Peralta and the Rays’ pitching staff. Doubles by Caleb Durbin and Roman Anthony gave the Red Sox their one run in the second, but they were stymied from there. They had chances!
- Second inning after Anthony’s two-out double: Mickey Gasper lineout to center
- Fourth inning with runners on first and second, one out: Story strikeout, Durbin popout
- Fifth inning with runner on second, one out: Anthony groundout, Gasper strikeout
- Sixth inning with runners on first and second, two out: Durbin fly out to left
- Eighth inning after Adley Rutschman’s one-out double: Wilyer Abreu strikeout, Nick Sogard lineout
Even against lockdown Rays closer Bryan Baker, Boston had one last shot to take a late lead. After Story grounded out, Durbin lined a double down the left field line to put himself in scoring position for Jarren Duran. Durbin darted from second, however, and got thrown out stealing third. Duran promptly followed with a triple over DeLuca’s head in center. Isiah Kiner-Falefa bounced one to Junior Caminero at third to end the threat.
Granted a chance to walk it off, Tampa Bay didn’t waste it. Rather than blasting a homer to finish the game as he had twice earlier this homestand, Caminero began the ninth against Garrett Whitlock with a single to left. (A catwalk curtailed Durbin’s effort to catch a popup earlier in the AB.) DeLuca popped up, but Chandler Simpson grounded one through the six-hole for another hit. The runners moved up when catcher Connor Wong let a Whitlock sinker up bounce off his glove for a passed ball. Palacios ended the night with flare to center that fell in, securing the win for Tampa Bay. At least the Wild Card Series is also almost certainly going to be at Yankee Stadium now, I suppose.
AL Rock Fight
Cleveland Guardians (80-75) 12, The Athletics (61-94) 6
Two crooked numbers effectively decided Saturday’s affair with the A’s in a hurry. Tanner Bibee kind of stunk and would allow six runs in a dozen hits while failing to make through five, but it hardly mattered. Cleveland erased a 2-0 deficit in the first on a three-run shot from rookie Chase DeLauter and two-run homer by Angel Martinez. The A’s got one back in the third, only to see another five-spot from the Guardians on poor Jacob Lopez as David Fry, Austin Hedges, and Brayan Rocchio all delivered RBI doubles. Martinez later added a homer and an RBI single in a career-best four-hit day.
Chicago White Sox (79-76) 3, Detroit Tigers (73-82) 1
Cleveland’s win meant that Chicago was stuck at a game back in the AL Central in the best-case, but they did at least help push one of their Wild Card foes out of the picture with a win. Honestly, this was probably kind of a dud of a game for anyone who isn’t a White Sox fan, the lone highlights being Sean Burke’s six scoreless frames and Miguel Vargas’ sixth-inning solo shot to make it 3-1, Chicago (the other runs scored on an RBI single by Munetaka Murakami and a fifth-inning sac fly). Spencer Torkelson had a chance to tie the game with a homer following Hao-Yu Lee’s two-out single in the ninth, but he flew out to center to end it.
Milwaukee Brewers (97-58) 1, Baltimore Orioles (75-80) 0
Yeah, it’s time to stick a fork in the O’s. It was all but certain for awhile now, but Chicago’s win combined with Baltimore’s second-straight loss to Milwaukee means that the Orioles are four back with a week to play, plus multiple teams in front of them. Trevor Rogers was the hard-luck loser here while Baltimore got blanked on four hits and Rece Hinds lost a fly ball from Joey Ortiz in the sun, allowing him to triple and score on Gary Sánchez’s RBI grounder. Woof.
Texas Rangers (78-77) 6, Toronto Blue Jays (76-79) 1
The O’s aren’t the only bird that are all but shot down, either. Trade Deadline acquisition José Soriano coughed up an early homer to Josh Jung, beginning a five-inning, six-run outing that pushed Toronto three games out in the Wild Card and the Rangers into a one-game AL West lead over Houston. The only downside for Texas was that second-half surprise Cal Quantrill—who has a 1.75 ERA since re-entering the rotation in late July—left in the second with lat tightness, so old friend Jordan Montgomery picked up the slack in long relief, retiring 11 of the 12 hitters he faced with no hits allowed.
Atlanta Braves (91-64) 6, Houston Astros (77-78) 3
Houston and Texas have been wrestling all week over the prestigious “Who can win this horri-awful division with a .500-ish record” crown. Sunday it went to Texas with the Astros falling out of their tie for first place (remember that they own the tiebreaker). Isaac Paredes had put Houston ahead with a solo homer and an RBI knock in the third, but the Astros’ bullpen set that lead on fire. The big blow came off the bat of Ronald Acuña Jr., who belted a grand slam off Bryan Abreu in the seventh after AJ Blubaugh made a right mess of things.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox and Tampa Bay Rays head into Sunday’s series finale at Fenway Park with the three-game set knotted at one win apiece after Saturday’s 2-1 Rays victory.
Left-hander Patrick Sandoval takes the mound for Boston against Tampa Bay right-hander Griffin Jax, a matchup that carries extra weight with the regular season winding down and playoff positioning still in flux.
Interim manager Chad Tracy has kept the bulk of his starting nine intact, but he has made a modest yet noticeable adjustment involving outfielder Jarren Duran, via Underdog MLB.
After sitting out the series opener and batting eighth on Saturday, Duran will slide up one spot into the seventh hole. He will hit in front of Isaiah Kiner-Falefa and Nate Eaton while remaining in center field, the position he has occupied since injuries to Ceddanne Rafaela and Eli White opened the job.
The rest of the order features Roman Anthony in left, Mickey Gasper at designated hitter, Adley Rutschman behind the plate, Trevor Story at shortstop, Nick Sogard at first, and Cooper Durbin at third.
The move comes during a difficult individual season for Duran. Entering Sunday he is hitting .206 in 144 games, with 65 runs, 110 hits, 20 home runs and 69 RBIs. His slugging percentage sits at .364 and his OPS at .626.
Speculation about a possible trade lingered for weeks before the August 4 deadline, yet Duran remained in a Red Sox uniform and has continued to receive regular playing time as the club pushes toward October.
Boston sits at 84-71 with seven games left and occupies what currently looks like the second American League Wild Card spot. Should the standings hold, the Red Sox would open the postseason on the road in a best-of-three Wild Card series against the New York Yankees.
Every remaining game, including Sunday’s finale against a familiar division rival, therefore carries playoff implications.
Tracy’s decision to bump Duran up in the order is a small tactical shift rather than a wholesale overhaul, but it signals a willingness to tinker as the club tries to generate more consistent offense down the stretch.
Whether the extra spot in the lineup produces results remains to be seen.
Duran’s season-long struggles have been well documented, yet he has shown flashes of the power and speed that once made him a fixture in the middle of Boston’s order.
A productive afternoon against Jax and the Rays would give the Red Sox a series victory and a bit of momentum heading into the final week.
With the calendar now late September and the postseason picture still taking shape, even incremental lineup changes can feel significant.

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Richie Palacios dropped a blooper into shallow right in the ninth inning to score Junior Caminero and give the Tampa Bay Rays a 2-1 victory over the Boston Red Sox on Saturday.
Tampa Bay, which has three walk-off wins on its current homestand, lowered its magic number to clinch the AL East to five games. The second-place Yankees are in Arizona on Saturday night.
Prior to Palacios’ single, the Rays were 0 for 17 with runners in scoring position over the first two games of the series. The postseason-bound Rays, who’ve won seven of their last eight, capitalized on two fortuitous bounces in the ninth.
First, Caminero’s foul popup bounced off the Tropicana Field catwalk and out of the reach of third baseman Caleb Durbin. Caminero then lined the next pitch from Garrett Whitlock (7-2) into left. Three batters later, after Chandler Simpson singled, Connor Wong’s passed ball moved Caminero to third.
Bidding to clinch a wild-card berth, the Red Sox squandered a prime opportunity in the top of the ninth.
Facing closer Bryan Baker (4-2) in a tie game, Boston got a double from Caleb Durbin and a triple from Jarren Duran. However, Nick Fortes threw out Durbin stealing third before Duran’s triple, and Caminero made a stellar play at third base to retire Isiah Kiner-Falefa, stranding Duran.
Boston also wasted a phenomenal effort from starter Brayan Bello, who matched a career high with 11 strikeouts. In eight innings, he allowed five hits, one run and no walks. Red Sox closer Aroldis Chapman (lat tightness) was unavailable.
The Red Sox took a 1-0 lead with doubles from Durbin and Roman Anthony in the third inning. Trevor Story extended his hitting streak to 10 games with a sixth-inning single.
Jonathan Aranda tied it with an opposite-field solo homer on the first pitch of the Rays’ fourth.
The Rays are an MLB-best 25-14 in one-run games.
Boston could have clinched a playoff berth with a win combined with a loss by either the Rangers or Astros. Both of those teams were seven games behind the Red Sox with eight games remaining entering Saturday.
UP NEXT
Right-hander Griffin Jax (7-10, 3.80 ERA) gets the nod for the Rays on Sunday in the series finale. Boston had not announced a starter.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

20 Sep 2026, 04:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Kim Klement Neitzel)
Richie Palacios produced a two-out, walk-off single in the ninth inning as the Tampa Bay Rays edged the Boston Red Sox 2-1 on Saturday afternoon in St. Petersburg, Fla., to even their final home series of the regular season.
Against Garrett Whitlock (7-2), Palacios looped a 1-2 sinker into shallow right to score Junior Caminero as the Rays (94-60) hit their third walk-off winner during the nine-game homestand.
Jonathan Aranda homered while Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson posted two hits apiece as Tampa Bay improved to 7-1 on the homestand.
Bidding for a fifth consecutive win over five starts, Freddy Peralta received no decision after yielding just one run on four hits over 5 2/3 innings that took 97 pitches. He struck out six and walked two.
Caleb Durbin stroked two doubles and scored for the Red Sox (84-71), who lost for the first time in three games.
Starting pitcher Brayan Bello went a season-best eight innings and allowed one run on five hits with a career high-tying 11 strikeouts.
The Rays got an out with the infield drawn in and appeared to escape trouble in the third. Then Roman Anthony, who homered and had three RBIs in Friday's 4-2 win in the opener, remained hot and made it 1-0 with a two-out double that scored Durbin.
Cedric Mullins laid down a bunt single and reached second on Durbin's throwing error to open the third, but he was picked off and caught trying to steal third on Jorge Mateo's failed sacrifice bunt.
In the fourth, Aranda tied it 1-all when he rocked his 22nd homer to left field as he took Bello's 97 m.p.h. four-seam fastball the opposite way.
With Bello still in the game in the seventh, Hicks led off with a single and Simpson dropped one into right with no outs. Following a groundout and a fielder's choice, Bello ended the threat by whiffing Mullins on a foul tip.
Durbin lined his second double with one out in the ninth, but Hicks tossed him out trying to steal third. Jarren Duran followed with his fifth triple, but Isiah Kiner-Falefa grounded out to deep third to end the inning off Bryan Baker (4-2).
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
The MLB offseason is over a month away, but rumors are already spreading.
The Boston Red Sox are in the middle of one as it pertains to an outfielder.
Seattle Mariners LF Randy Arozarena is due to hit free agency after the conclusion of this year’s World Series, and Boston could make him a big offer, according to a Seattle reporter.
“(The Mariners are) going to lose their best offensive player. Randy Arozarena’s gonna be a free agent. I think we all know Randy would probably prefer to stay on the east coast,” The Seattle Times’ Ryan Divish said on Foul Territory on Friday. “I’m guessing Boston is ready to cut a huge check for him.”
Arozarena, 31, is having a career year for the Mariners. He was named an All-Star for the third time and is slashing .281/.377/.479 with an .856 OPS. He’s clubbed 25 home runs (two away from tying a career-high), scored 104 times, and driven in 63 runs across 147 games.
If he were on the 2026 Red Sox, he’d lead the club in runs and have the second-most homers behind Willson Contreras (27).
Arozarena, a Cuban native, was named the 2021 American League Rookie of the Year in 2021 as a member of the Tampa Bay Rays. The Rays dealt him to Seattle in 2024, but his time to choose his next team is coming up.
Divish said he doesn’t think the Mariners will “get in a bidding war” for Arozarena once he hits the market.
If Boston were to land the right-handed hitter, they’d likely have to pay up. Arozarena could earn over $20 million annually as he’ll surely seek out a lengthy contract.
On top of the finances, the Red Sox would have to make room on their roster for the slugger. The team currently has eight outfielders on its major-league roster (Ceddanne Rafaela, Masataka Yoshida, and Eli White are on the injured list).
White and Jahmai Jones, whom Boston picked up at the trade deadline earlier this year, are both arbitration-eligible after this season. The team could non-tender one of the two to make room as one of many possible moves in a hypothetical scenario involving adding Arozarena.
Additionally, the Red Sox have reportedly attempted to trade Jarren Duran several times over the last couple of years. They could give that another go this winter and let Arozarena — who also plays LF — take his place.
Designated hitter is also an option for Arozarena. He’s DHed minimally, but given his age and Boston’s crowded outfield, it could be feasible.
Based on his career, Arozarena would be a magnificent fit at Fenway Park. In 32 career games played in Boston, he’s slashing .278/.351/.481 with an .833 OPS, five HR, 12 doubles, and 19 RBI.
Arozarena is set to hit free agency at an incredibly uncertain time in the league’s history, though. A lockout looms when the current collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1, which would halt the ability for clubs to sign free agents.
Boston would need to move rather swiftly in acquiring Arozarena — and any other players on the trade and free agent markets— before that deadline, and until a new CBA is agreed upon. The latter could take an indefinite amount of time.

item.content:encoded:
Caleb Durbin managed to do exactly what you do not want to do as the go-ahead run.
The Boston Red Sox played Saturday against the division rival Tampa Bay Rays. In the top of the ninth inning at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla. with the score tied 1-1, the Boston infielder Durbin hit a one-out double to represent the winning run.
In the middle of the next at-bat by teammate Jarren Duran however, Durbin committed an inexplicable blunder — he decided to make a break for third base. Durbin was then easily thrown out for the second out of the inning.
Caleb Durbin is caught trying to steal 3rd and Junior Caminero is FIRED UP
We are still tied in the 9th!pic.twitter.com/wrriTXW1yj
Making matters even worse for Durbin was that Duran proceeded to smack a triple in his at-bat (but was stranded at third after Isiah Kiner-Falefa grounded out to end the half-inning). While Duran’s triple would have allowed Durbin to waltz home if he had simply stayed put, the baserunning error left the game tied and opened the door for the Rays to win the game in the bottom of the ninth inning on a walkoff RBI single by Richie Palacios.
It is hard to tell exactly what Durbin was thinking there. He was already in scoring position and also had a left-handed batter up at the plate (meaning that the catcher had an obstructed throw to third base). Though Durbin has stolen 19 bases so far this season, that was simply a risk completely unnecessary for him to take in that situation.
On the bright side, the 84-71 Red Sox do look to be locked into the second AL Wild Card spot at this point, which would have them open up the playoffs against the rival New York Yankees. But these are the types of moments that explain why Boston is a Wild Card team to begin with (similar to the time that they cost themselves four runs by botching a single challenge).

item.content:encoded:
La temporada regular de la MLB 2026 entra en su recta final y la pelea por los boletos a los Playoffs comienza a tomar forma. En medio de esta definición, varios peloteros mexicanos y mexicoamericanos mantienen vivas sus aspiraciones de llegar a la postemporada con sus respectivas organizaciones.
En la Liga Americana hay nombres que ya tienen prácticamente asegurado el escenario de octubre, mientras que otros todavía deben afrontar una intensa batalla por los puestos de comodín. Entre ellos aparecen jugadores que han tenido un papel importante durante la campaña y que buscan convertirse en representantes de México durante los Playoffs.
¿Qué mexicanos ya tienen encaminado su boleto?
Entre los jugadores que tienen su lugar asegurado destaca Jonathan Aranda, infielder tijuanense de los Tampa Bay Rays, franquicia que matemáticamente consiguió su clasificación a la postemporada y que se mantiene en la parte alta de la División Este de la Liga Americana.
Otro nombre que se encuentra en plena pelea es Jarren Durán, jardinero mexicoamericano de los Boston Red Sox. El pelotero forma parte de una novena que pelea por mantenerse en la zona de clasificación del joven circuito y que apunta a disputar la Serie de Comodines si consigue sostener su posición.
Por su parte, Alejandro Kirk continúa siendo una de las principales referencias mexicanas en las Grandes Ligas. El receptor de los Toronto Blue Jays afronta con su equipo una cerrada lucha por ingresar a los Playoffs de la Liga Americana, con cada partido de la recta final teniendo un peso importante en sus aspiraciones.
La pelea también está en la Liga Nacional
En el Viejo Circuito también hay varios peloteros con posibilidades de disputar la postemporada. Alek Thomas, jardinero mexicoamericano de los Arizona Diamondbacks, se encuentra involucrado en la cerrada pelea por los últimos boletos de comodín de la Liga Nacional.
Los San Diego Padres también cuentan con representación mexicana con Jeremiah Estrada, relevista mexicoamericano que forma parte del bullpen de una organización que se mantiene en puestos que actualmente entregarían un boleto a la postemporada mediante el comodín.
Mientras tanto, Javier Assad vive una situación favorable con los Chicago Cubs. El pitcher tijuanense forma parte de una novena que tiene prácticamente encaminada su clasificación, con los Cachorros ubicados en una posición privilegiada dentro de la carrera por los Playoffs de la Liga Nacional.
Otros jugadores también permanecen atentos a la definición de la temporada. Taijuan Walker, con los Philadelphia Phillies, así como JoJo Romero y Ramón Urías, con los St. Louis Cardinals, buscan mantener a sus respectivos equipos dentro de la conversación por los últimos lugares disponibles en la Nacional.
